subject: Request for one-time remediation credit due to model-offload timeline slip
messages:
From: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@veridian.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-11T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Urgent: impact of delayed on-prem model-offload on launch

Marcus —

Quick note from the Veridian launch team: our engineering lead Suresh confirmed this morning that the missing on-prem model-offload hooks (the persistent-KV prefetch we discussed) are blocking our production inference path. We were scheduled to flip the feature flag next week for the pilot and that now won't happen unless we get an alternative.

This delay impacts our compliance milestone and the go-live we synchronized with our payor partners. We need to discuss commercial remediation — specifically a short-term credit or discount while we wait for the feature, and a clear timeline from Redwood so we can communicate to our stakeholders.

Attaching a one-page impact summary for context. Can you loop in product and legal?

—Alex
Veridian Health
attachments: production-impact-summary.pdf (page stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-11T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: impact of delayed on-prem model-offload on launch

Team — forwarding Veridian. They just raised a commercial ask tied to the on-prem model-offload timeline (persistent KV/prefetch). High level: customer is asking for a short credit while the missing runtime capability blocks their pilot.

Ask: 1) Product (Lauren + Aditya) — confirm the earliest realistic ETA for the offload hooks and whether there is a safe patch/bandaid we can offer in the next 7–10 days. 2) Sales (Vanessa) — need guidance on a commercial remediation range I can offer immediately (we should give them something pre-approved if possible). 3) CS (Monica) — please capture impact details and consequences to the go-live schedule.

I attached their impact summary and a quick skeleton of a remediation proposal (spreadsheet). I think we should aim for an executable, conditional credit (timeboxed, tied to milestones) rather than an open discount.

I will draft a proposal once product confirms ETA. Low noise please — Alex asked for a short timeline to share with execs at Veridian.

—Marcus
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199
attachments: production-impact-summary.pdf, remediation-credit-proposal-v1.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-11T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: impact of delayed on-prem model-offload on launch

Marcus / team —

Thanks for flagging. Short answer: the persistent-KV prefetch/offload hooks are scoped for the next minor runtime release (R-1.14), which was dependent on kernel alignment that slipped last sprint. Current realistic ETA for a beta build is 2028-01-25; GA would be early Feb, barring regressions. We can prioritize a hotfix branch and push a limited patch for Veridian but that will require engineering capacity and a signed operational variance (we'll need to tag the build and limit it to their Dedicated cluster).

Workarounds: 1) temporary prefix sharding + manual warm-up script (lower throughput, higher token cost) — engineering can provide instructions within 48 hours; 2) we can commit to the hotfix branch with a dedicated QA slot and an agreed rollback plan. Neither is as clean as the offload hooks, but both will unblock some traffic.

If we go with the hotfix path, we will need a short commercial remediation (customer asks) and sign-off from finance + legal to ship a limited release.

I will schedule a 30-minute sync with Aditya and the engineering lead tomorrow to scope the hotfix effort.

—Lauren
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed conditional remediation: draft for exec approval

Vanessa / Monica —

Per product ETA and the potential hotfix path, I drafted a conditional remediation we can pitch to Veridian:

- One-time credit equal to 20% of Veridian's committed monthly credit for the first month post-launch, applied as a bill credit.
- If we deliver the hotfix and Veridian flips within 14 days of the hotfix availability, credit reduces to 10%.
- Credit only applies to committed spend (not overage).
- Customer signs a short amendment acknowledging the limited-release nature of the hotfix and agreeing to a rollback policy.

Rationale: balances commercial goodwill with incentive for quick validation; keeps exposure capped. I attached a spreadsheet with the dollar math and a proposed amendment template.

Need: executive approval to offer up to 25% one-time credit (so Sales can negotiate up to that band), and Legal to draft the amendment. Also need Finance to confirm the accounting treatment (we should be able to apply as a billing credit).

Can you confirm approval or provide redlines? If we have approval, I will send to Alex today with the hotfix plan attached.

—Marcus
attachments: remediation-credit-proposal-v1.xlsx, timeline_gantt.png
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-12T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed conditional remediation: draft for exec approval

Marcus —

Approved with edits. Executive decision: authorize up to 22% one-time credit on the first monthly committed bill as a goodwill remediation, conditional on the hotfix delivery plan and the signed amendment. Key conditions:

1) Credit cap: $75k maximum exposure.
2) Hotfix acceptance test must be executed in Veridian's staging within 7 business days of release.
3) Credit is applied only if Veridian remains a customer for at least 90 days post-flip (to avoid churn exposure).

Legal — please fast-track a concise amendment (one page) that references the hotfix, acceptance criteria, rollback, and the limited support window. Finance — confirm we can apply this as a billing credit without impacting our revenue recognition materially; copy me on the confirmation.

Marcus — once Legal sends the amendment, send to Alex and propose a 48-hour window for Veridian to sign and schedule the hotfix deployment. Let's close this quickly.

—Vanessa
VP Sales, East
Redwood Inference
